character_facts: Aghora is portrayed by others as temporarily vulnerable because of advanced pregnancy.
The conspirators aim to seize the throne and are willing to arrange murder to do it.
The recruited woman values power and mobility tied to her kantylopter.
The recruited woman believes she is 'nothing' without her kantylopter.
The conspirators have access to advanced cloning capabilities or to someone who can perform cloning.
characters_present: Aghora, the current Metabaron (discussed, not shown directly)
A dark-haired female warrior or raider being recruited
continuity_links: This page sets up an assassination attempt against Aghora.
The throne succession or control of the empire is tied to Aghora's survival.
The cloned kantylopter is presented as the inducement meant to secure the woman's cooperation.
dialogue_meaning: The conspirators identify a narrow window of weakness in Aghora's late pregnancy.
They argue that pregnancy prevents Aghora from using some usual combat abilities and slows her movement.
They offer the woman a political and military reward in exchange for assassinating Aghora.
The promised reward includes legal authority for violent plunder under imperial command.
The woman explains that losing her kantylopter left her effectively helpless.
The conspirators counter her objection by unveiling a cloned replacement grown from recovered cells.
locations: An interior chamber where conspirators confer
Outer space beside a large structure or ship
A room or holding area where the woman is shown the cloned specimen
lore_facts: At this moment in the story, Aghora is nine months pregnant.
Because of the fetus, Aghora cannot use her mini-bombs.
Aghora is said to be able to defend herself only with her Metablade in her current condition.
There is an imperial forces hierarchy with a role of supreme commander.
Minor planets can be legally raided under imperial authority, according to the conspirators' offer.
A kantylopter is an important source of power or capability for the recruited woman.
A cell from a destroyed kantylopter can be used to clone an identical specimen.
plot_events: Conspirators explain that Aghora, the current Metabaron, is female and nine months pregnant.
They describe Aghora as physically limited: unable to move quickly, unable to use mini-bombs safely, and able to defend herself only with her Metablade.
The conspirators propose that the woman kill Aghora so they can seize the throne.
As payment, they offer to make the woman supreme commander of the imperial forces, enabling her to raid minor planets for profit.
The woman says she was rendered powerless when the Empire destroyed her kantylopter.
The conspirators reveal that they recovered a cell from the destroyed being and cloned an identical specimen.
The woman reacts with visible surprise to the cloned creature.
uncertainties: Some dialogue is small and slightly hard to read, so wording-level precision may be imperfect.

The exact nature of the object shown in the space panel is unclear from this page alone, though it appears connected to the negotiation.
visual_summary: Grotesque cybernetic courtiers or conspirators discuss the vulnerability of the current Metabaron, Aghora. A space panel separates their proposal from a later scene where they negotiate with a dark-haired woman in revealing armor. She says the Empire left her powerless by destroying her kantylopter. The conspirators then present a cloned replacement specimen in a case, shocking her.
